ownership.value: Private — formerly public (NYSE: SAVE). Ownership passed from public shareholders to former creditors (institutional bondholders/debtholders) when Spirit emerged from its first Chapter 11 on March 12, 2025 via exchange of $795 million of funded debt for equity plus a $296.1 million equity rights offering (7,770,054 shares issued to ERO participants). After the second Chapter 11 filing (Aug 29, 2025) and the May 2, 2026 shutdown, the debtor estate is in court-supervised wind-down controlled by creditors and DIP lenders; no PE sponsor or founder owner.

debt_events.summary: Spirit filed for Chapter 11 protection in the Southern District of New York with $3.6 billion in total outstanding debt; came after JetBlue merger blocked in court and $2.5bn+ cumulative losses since 2020.

Launched $350.0 million equity rights offering ($14.00/share) in the first bankruptcy; closed at emergence on 2025-03-12 with $296,107,812 of consideration (7,770,054 shares + 13,380,504 warrants to ERO participants).

Emerged from first Chapter 11 via a consensual deleveraging that equitized approximately $795 million of funded debt; 2024 DIP facility ($300M) and $300M revolving credit facility repaid in full at emergence; new $275M exit revolving credit facility (matures 2026, reduced to $250M on 2026-09-30).

Credit-card processor (USB) amendments: Spirit transferred an additional $50 million cash to a pledged account and agreed to up-to-$3 million/day holdbacks until the processor was fully collateralized, in exchange for extending the card processing agreement to Dec 31, 2027 — a sign counterparties were pulling back credit.

Spirit warned it might not survive a year without significantly more cash and borrowed the entire $275 million available under its revolving credit facility; going-concern risk disclosed with Q2 2025 results.

Filed second Chapter 11 in under a year (Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc., Case No. 25-11897, Bankruptcy Court SDNY), carrying $2.4 billion long-term debt and $1 billion negative free cash flow at Q2 2025; lessor AerCap had terminated aircraft leases.

Bankruptcy Court approved a final order authorizing a multi-draw senior secured super-priority priming DIP facility of up to $1.2 billion, including a roll-up of pre-petition secured notes up to $750 million.

Filed a plan of reorganization, disclosure statement and restructuring support agreement with consenting DIP lenders; later pivoted from reorganization to wind-down, seeking to auction LaGuardia slots, corporate campus, loyalty program and equipment, and to sell/abandon 28 owned aircraft and 18 spare engines.

Ceased all flight operations at 3:00 a.m. EDT after bailout negotiations between creditors and the Trump administration (a ~$500 million proposal) collapsed; blamed sharply rising fuel costs from the 2026 Iran war on top of existing distress; company began an orderly wind-down and liquidation under Bankruptcy Court supervision.

Judge Sean H. Lane approved the debtors' wind-down procedures and granted aircraft lease rejection and sale motions; U.S. Trustee's suggestion to convert to Chapter 7 was not pressed; Broward County (FLL operator) asserted liens on aircraft for postpetition administrative claims.

Court-set claims bar dates: general proofs of claim due Jan 27, 2026, governmental units Feb 25, 2026, and pre-wind-down administrative expense claims July 27, 2026 — mass claims process against the estate.

credit_ratings.summary: S&P Global Ratings downgraded Spirit to 'CCC' from 'CCC+', outlook negative, citing approaching 2025 maturities ($1.1bn loyalty bonds due Sep 2025, $500M convertibles 2026), a 'less than adequate' liquidity position, and a view that a distressed exchange was likely within 12 months.

Fitch Ratings downgraded Spirit Airlines to 'CCC-' from 'CCC+' citing mounting operational losses, deteriorating liquidity and heightened default risk; also downgraded Spirit's loyalty-program debt to 'CCC-' from 'B-' (recovery rating RR4 from RR3).

Moody's Ratings downgraded Spirit two notches deeper into junk to Caa3, citing 'higher than expected cash burn'; forecast Spirit would burn more than $500 million of cash in 2025; noted just $408 million unrestricted cash at Q2 2025 and the fully tapped $275 million revolver (matures March 2028); followed Spirit's going-concern warning.

Rating trajectory over ~2 years: B2 (2023) to Caa3 (2025), a collapse across five loss-making of six quarters; S&P projected a $600 million free cash flow deficit for 2025; negative outlooks signalled further downgrades.

output.risk_rationale: Spirit Airlines is the highest-risk counterparty profile possible short of full dissolution: it filed Chapter 11 twice (Nov 2024 and Aug 29, 2025), was rated deep-junk (Fitch CCC-, Moody's Caa3) with going-concern doubt disclosed in its Q3 2025 Form 10-Q, drew its entire $275 million revolver and pledged extra collateral to its credit-card processor before ceasing ALL flight operations on May 2, 2026 after a ~$500 million federal bailout proposal failed. It is now in a court-supervised wind-down and liquidation (wind-down order approved May 5, 2026; LaGuardia slots, loyalty program and campus up for auction; >4,850 Florida WARN layoffs), so any receivable, prepaid balance or contract with Spirit is a claim in a distressed estate with likely severe recovery shortfalls for unsecured creditors.

distress_signals.summary: CEO Ted Christie — a 13-year veteran — exited and left the board weeks after emergence from the first bankruptcy; CCO Matt Klein stepped down immediately; an 'office of the president' (CFO Fred Cromer, COO John Bendoraitis, GC Thomas Canfield) ran the company until Dave Davis was named CEO.

Going-concern warning: management disclosed 'substantial doubt' about ability to continue as a going concern just months after emerging from bankruptcy; repeated as substantial-doubt language in the Q3 2025 Form 10-Q.

Network and workforce shrinkage: discontinued service in 11 U.S. cities from October (Albuquerque, Birmingham, Boise, Chattanooga, Columbia, Oakland, Sacramento, San Jose, San Diego, Portland, Salt Lake City); furloughed ~270 pilots from Nov 1 and downgraded 140 captains to first officers from Oct 1; later confirmed 1,800 flight-attendant furloughs (nearly one-third of cabin crew) by Dec 1, 2025.
Spirit cut ~150 corporate/market jobs and exited several markets as part of the second restructuring.
An Examiner was appointed in the Chapter 11 case (SDNY), an indicator of contested, complex proceedings.

Reports that Spirit was at risk of imminent liquidation as jet-fuel prices surged in the 2026 Iran war; by April 18 it sought a federal bailout and the administration considered acquiring a controlling stake.

Shut down entirely: flights grounded by 3 a.m., Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced the shutdown, employee health insurance ended that day, and Florida WARN notices showed more than 4,850 layoffs (2,529 at FLL, 551 at Dania Beach support center, 181 at MIA, 796 at MCO plus 796 at MCO inflight/ops center).
Fleet shrank from 214 aircraft pre-bankruptcy toward a planned 76 by mid-August 2026 (active fleet roughly 120-130 in early 2026), with international routes slashed — a drastic operational retreat.

payment_behaviour.summary: Its own credit-card processor demanded additional credit support: Spirit transferred $50 million cash to a pledged account and allowed up to $3 million/day holdbacks until the processor was fully collateralized — direct evidence counterparties feared non-payment and cut Spirit's effective credit.
Aircraft lessor AerCap terminated aircraft leases in the run-up to the second Chapter 11 filing; Spirit later sought court approval to reject remaining aircraft leases.

Broward County, operator of Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport, objected to the wind-down stay and asserted liens on Spirit aircraft at the airport to secure postpetition administrative claims; numerous trade counterparties, airport authorities, lessors and insurers forced modifications to the proposed wind-down order.

Claims process opened against the estate: general proofs of claim bar date Jan 27, 2026, governmental units Feb 25, 2026, pre-wind-down administrative expense claims July 27, 2026 (Epiq is claims agent; vendor information page hosted at spiritrestructuring.com) — an invitation for mass creditor claims including unpaid vendors.
